definition: Klüver–Bucy syndrome is a neurobehavioral disorder linked to dysfunction in both medial temporal lobes. It can involve unusually strong oral or touch-based exploration, hypersexuality, overeating, memory problems, unusual calmness, and difficulty recognizing objects or faces, and it may occur after brain injury or with conditions such as infections, Alzheimer disease, Pick disease, or cerebrovascular disorders.
